🚀 Just published my new SQL case study project on GitHub!
💳 Title: Credit Card Transactions Analysis using SQL
📂 Repo: https://lnkd.in/d57X-E5s
🔍 What I did:
• Cleaned and imported a real-world credit card dataset from Kaggle into SQL Server
• Normalized column names and optimized data types
• Solved 10 business questions using SQL, including:
• Top cities by spending
• Gender-based spend analysis
• Expense-type trends
• Month-over-month growth
• Weekend vs weekday behavior
🛠️ Tools: SQL Server, T-SQL, Window Functions, CTEs, Aggregations
📈 Sample insight:
“Platinum + Travel saw the highest MoM growth in Jan 2014 🚀”
Check out the full project on GitHub:
👉 https://lnkd.in/dyN4bTAv
🙏 Special thanks to Ankit Bansal for sharing the case study and being a constant source of learning and guidance throughout this project!
💬 I'd love to hear your feedback or suggestions!
Dhaval Patel Hemanand Vadivel Shashank Singh 🇮🇳 NamasteSQL

ai_analysis.summary: The post describes a GitHub case study that imports a Kaggle credit card transaction dataset, described as real-world, into SQL Server. The project cleans the data by normalizing column names and optimizing data types, then uses SQL to answer ten business questions about spending, customer attributes, expense types, monthly growth, and weekday-versus-weekend behavior. The post names T-SQL, window functions, CTEs, and aggregations as tools used and reports that the Platinum and Travel category had the highest month-over-month growth in January 2014.
